views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Send the Mnuchin-Lighthizer-Ross delegation into the Beijing talks without imposing the proposed Section 301 list and without adding the extra $100 billion Trump floated after China's April 4 list. Keep the ZTE denial order and the 301 comment/hearing process intact as leverage, and refuse a purchases-only package that leaves Made in China 2025, forced tech transfer, and investment restrictions untouched. Do not roll anything back until Beijing puts structural offers on the table that can be verified.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is mildly an opportunity, not a crisis. The USTR 301 report (2018-03-22) and the proposed ~$50B list targeting aerospace, ICT, robotics and machinery (2018-04-03) put US complaints about IP theft and industrial policy on a concrete track, and the April 16 ZTE denial order is described as a near-operational shutdown of China's second-largest telecom vendor—asymmetric pressure China cannot easily match. US macro is still healthy: Michigan sentiment 98, industrial production rising, VIX back near 16 after the late-March spike, and the goods deficit actually narrower on the latest print. That is not the +0.5 "material GDP drag" case. The offset is real but contained: China already levied ~$3B on pork/fruit/nuts (2018-04-02) and proposed 25% on ~$50B including soybeans, autos and aircraft (2018-04-04), with soybeans alone ~$14.6B and concentrated in Trump-won farm states. Those lists are mostly still proposed (301 hearing set for May 15), so the dispute has not yet become a tariff cascade. Action should stay near zero because talks are launching this week (Liu He vs Mnuchin/Lighthizer/Ross/Navarro/Kudlow) with slim odds of a structural deal and explicit Chinese refusal to bargain Made in China 2025 or a $100B deficit cut. Escalating tariffs or another entity-list hit now would likely freeze the talks and accelerate soybean/auto retaliation before the 301 record is even closed; conceding purchases or a partial rollback would cash in ZTE/301 leverage for measures Beijing was already advertising (JV phase-outs, auto tariff cuts, more commodity buys). Negotiate, keep the instruments live, and judge any offer against structural IP/tech terms—not a one-year export bump.
key_factors: Section 301 findings and proposed $50B list are live but not yet imposed; comment/hearing process still open
ZTE seven-year denial order is the strongest non-tariff card and is already biting
China has answered with $3B in-force 232 retaliation and a proposed $50B list aimed at soybeans, autos, and aircraft
US real economy and risk markets are not showing a trade-war shock as of early May 2018
Beijing talks are starting with low expectations and a split US delegation; purchases-only offers should be rejected
Farm-belt political exposure is the main US vulnerability if talks fail and lists go live

sources_cited.excerpt: USTR releases Section 301 report finding China's IP/tech-transfer practices unreasonable or discriminatory. Trump signs presidential memorandum directing tariffs on Chinese imports, a WTO case, and investment restrictions.
USTR publishes proposed Section 301 tariff list: ~1,300 Chinese product lines (~$50B), targeting aerospace, ICT, robotics, machinery and related sectors. Public comment process opens.
China announces proposed retaliatory tariffs on ~$50B of US goods (including soybeans, automobiles, and aircraft) in response to the Section 301 list.
US Commerce Department bans ZTE from buying US components (denial order). ZTE faces operational shutdown. Major non-tariff escalation.
China imposes retaliatory tariffs on about $3B of US goods (pork, fruit, nuts, wine, and related items) in response to Section 232 steel/aluminum tariffs.
University of Michigan consumer sentiment still high at 98 (May 2018 print) after 101.4 in March—no collapse in household confidence.
VIX closed 15.97 on 2018-05-02, well off the 23–25 readings around the March 22 memorandum and early-April tariff lists.
US goods trade deficit narrowed to -$66.6B on the latest print from -$71.4B in Dec 2017; dispute not yet showing up as a widening external shock.

Most likely outcome of the Mnuchin-Liu He talks is an agreement to keep talking; breakthrough on China's structural policies viewed as highly unlikely; Chinese official said Beijing will not negotiate core interests including Made in China 2025.

US team of Mnuchin, Lighthizer, Ross, Navarro and Kudlow arriving for Thursday talks; ZTE ban effectively cripples the firm; China still believed the dispute could be resolved by buying more US products.
China's proposed 25% on soybeans hits a $14.6B export flow (over a third of the US crop); Trump won 8 of 10 top soybean states; he also instructed USTR to consider $100B more in 301 tariffs.
